title: From gas exchange to Fatmax
text: Fat oxidation measured directly; inferred oxygen uptake (VO2) carbon dioxide output (VCO2). Oxidising 1 g glucose consumes 0.746 L O2 produces 0.746 L CO2, respiratory exchange ratio (RER) 1.00; oxidising 1 g fat consumes 2.03 L O2 produces 1.43 L CO2, RER 0.70 (Frayn 1983, Table 1). Solving two balances two unknowns gives stoichiometric equations turn VO2 VCO2 grams carbohydrate (CHO) fat (FAT) oxidised per minute (Frayn 1983). package uses urinary nitrogen set zero, .e. ignores protein oxidation. inference fails high intensity, CO2 released bicarbonate pool buffer lactate adds CO2 produced oxidation (Jeukendrup Wallis 2005). graded test participant exercises steps increasing intensity, classically 3 min 35 W increments (Achten et al. 2002); Chenevière et al. (2009) used 3 min 20 W. Plotted intensity, fat oxidation rises, reaches peak, maximal fat oxidation rate (MFO, g/min), falls towards zero. intensity peak Fatmax, expressed %VO2max. sample Achten et al. title: From gas exchange to Fatmax
text: default method, P3, fits third-degree polynomial FAT %VO2max. Fatmax root derivative gives highest FAT within measured range, MFO fitted FAT root.
code: p3 <- lm(FAT ~ porc_VO2 + I(porc_VO2^2) + I(porc_VO2^3), data = steps) b <- coef(p3) roots <- Re(polyroot(c(b[2], 2 * b[3], 3 * b[4])))           # FAT'(x) = 0 roots <- roots[roots >= min(steps$porc_VO2) & roots <= max(steps$porc_VO2)] fat_at <- function(x) predict(p3, newdata = data.frame(porc_VO2 = x)) Fatmax <- roots[which.max(fat_at(roots))] MFO_hand <- unname(fat_at(Fatmax)) c(MFO = MFO_hand, Fatmax = Fatmax, R2 = summary(p3)$r.squared) #>        MFO     Fatmax         R2  #>  0.3167120 36.1703807  0.9711575

what: 5. Fat oxidation kinetics with the SIN model
title: From gas exchange to Fatmax
text: Chenevière et al. (2009) describe whole curve, normalised %MFO, sine function three parameters (eq. [14]): %MFO(x)=sin⁡{[π1/sπ+2d(Kx+d+t)]s},K=π100,x=%V̇O2max.\%\text{MFO}(x) = \sin\left\{\left[\frac{\pi^{1/s}}{\pi + 2d}\,(Kx + d + t)\right]^{s}\right\}, \qquad K = \frac{\pi}{100},\quad x = \%\dot{V}\text{O}_{2\max}. d = 0, s = 1 t = 0 half sine wave peak 50 %VO2max zeros 0 100 %VO2max. d (dilatation) widens (d > 0) narrows (d < 0) curve; s (symmetry) skews : s > 1 rightward asymmetry 0 < s < 1 leftward one (Chenevière et al. 2009); t (translation) shifts whole curve left (t > 0) right (t < 0). MFO_kinetics() fits model nonlinear least squares directly observed steps, normalised highest observed step, without smoothing, Chenevière et al. (2009) . Fatmax_SIN Fatmin come closed forms eq. [14]; Fatmin second zero curve (set fatmin_threshold use proportion MFO instead).  MFO_kinetics() fits every row receives, SIN inherits choices made MFO(). example last step RER > 1: truncated zero point curve, excluded . RER_cutoff = 1 gives selection Chenevière et al. (2009), averaged steps RER ≤ 1.0. SIN parameters; Fatmax_SIN Fatmin %VO2max. single step moves Fatmin several points , setting must reported. fewer 4 steps SIN fitted (convergence = FALSE); 4–5 steps fitted warning, 6 steps recommended.

title: MFO 0.2.0
text: MFO() gains method choose curve-fitting method: "P3" (third-degree polynomial, new default), "P2" "MRER". Version 0.1.0 always used second-degree polynomial. MFO() gains author = "Peronnet" (Péronnet & Massicotte, 1991) addition "Frayn" "Jeukendrup". New protocol arguments MFO() MFOs(): step_duration (default 180 s) steady_state_duration (default 60 s). New artefact handling: RER_cutoff removes steps RER threshold; negative_FAT chooses whether negative fat oxidation truncated 0, excluded kept. New outputs MFO(): Fatmax zone (fat oxidation within 10 % MFO), crossover point, heart rate Fatmax Fatmax %HRmax (HRmax), MFO relative body mass (body_mass) fat-free mass (fat_free_mass), R_squared / RMSE fit. MFO_kinetics() now returns standard errors d, s t, FatMax_SIN, Fatmin, R_squared, RMSE convergence flag, handles fitting failures without stopping. MFOs() passes new MFO() arguments gains output_format ("xlsx", "csv" "rds"). Internal helper average breath--breath data fixed intervals.
